messages.subject: Specification of the hyperpriors
parts:
From what I have read in th INLA description and examples, the default prior for the log precision is logGamma(1.0,0.001). Is it possible to change this prior and use a prior for the standard deviation (std) as U(0,100)  and define the precision as 1/(std)^2? This is often used in WinBUGS so I was wandering if it can be implemented in INLA as well.
Also, can we specify hyperparameters of order higher than 2?
Thank you,
Georgiana

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specification of the hyperpriors
parts: You can change priors, see the www page for a list of priors and how to change dem. The truncated uniform prior is not implemented, but the flat prior is. Note that the prior is defined on theta and in the internal scale, like log precision etc.
